task.title: Bring your own AI key: per-user provider, key and model for all AI features
task.description:
## Decision (owner, 2026-11-18)

Every AI feature in the app runs on a key the user supplies. This replaces the deployment-level key that recipe import uses today, and covers the AI features the Weekly Meal Planner adds (nutrition estimates, describing an eat-out meal). Because users pay for their own calls, sign-ups do not need limiting.

## What the owner chose

- A user picks one of three providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter), pastes a key and chooses a model, mirroring today's deployment setting (`RECIPE_AGENT_PROVIDER`, `RECIPE_AGENT_MODEL`, the three `*_API_KEY` variables; see `convex/lib/recipeModel.ts`).
- No deployment fallback: without a key, AI features are off for that user.

## To work out in the design

- Where keys are stored and how they are protected (encrypted at rest, never returned to the client after saving, removable).
- What recipe import does for a user with no key: link import, the forwarded-email inbox and manual entry each need a defined behaviour and message.
- Validating a key and model when saved, and the error copy when a call later fails (bad key, no credit, model without structured output).
- Whether the deployment variables are removed or ignored, and the README and `.env.example` changes.
- Relation to the backlog story "Customizable OpenRouter routing and model selection for recipe imports", which may fold into the per-user settings.

## Order

Needed before the planner's AI helpers. The planner's non-AI parts do not depend on it.
